questions.q: What question does Azure RBAC answer, as distinct from Microsoft Entra ID?
options: What is a given identity allowed to do to a specific resource, resource group, subscription, or management group
Who is allowed to sign into the Azure portal at all
Which users exist in the directory and what groups they belong to
How billing is split across subscriptions
questions.explain: Azure RBAC is resource-scoped authorization, answering what an identity can do to a specific resource — a narrower question than Entra ID's directory-level "who can manage the tenant itself."

questions.q: Where does the Access control (IAM) blade appear in Azure?
options: On every resource, resource group, and subscription
Only on the root management group
Only inside Microsoft Entra ID's admin center
Only on virtual machines, not on other resource types
questions.explain: Access control (IAM) is the center of gravity for Azure RBAC at any scope — it appears on resources, resource groups, and subscriptions, each showing Check access, Role assignments, Roles, and Deny assignments.

questions.q: What are the three tabs of the Add role assignment wizard, in order?
options: Role, Members, Review + assign
Members, Role, Confirm
Scope, Role, Billing
Search, Select, Submit
questions.explain: Every Azure RBAC assignment goes through the same three-tab wizard: pick the Role, pick the Members it applies to, then Review + assign to confirm.

questions.q: What's the difference between "Job function roles" and "Privileged administrator roles" on the Role tab?
options: Job function roles are scoped to a specific task (like Reader); privileged administrator roles are broad, high-risk roles like Owner or Contributor
Job function roles can only be assigned to groups; privileged administrator roles can only be assigned to individuals
There is no meaningful difference -- they are two names for the same role catalog
Privileged administrator roles can only be used in Azure Government regions
questions.explain: Job function roles are scoped to one task (Reader, Storage Blob Data Reader), while privileged administrator roles like Owner and Contributor grant much broader access and carry correspondingly higher risk if over-assigned.

questions.q: Why does assigning a role at the resource group level, rather than per resource, matter for a team that needs access to many storage accounts?
options: The role assignment is inherited by everything in the resource group automatically, including any new storage account added later, without repeating the assignment
Resource-group-level assignments only work for read-only roles, never for write access
It has no practical benefit over assigning the role to each storage account individually
Resource-group-level role assignments expire automatically after 90 days
questions.explain: Scope inheritance means a role assigned at the resource group level applies to every resource inside it now and in the future — one assignment instead of one per resource, and no manual step needed when a new resource is added.
